5.	Five-year Accident History:
There have been no accidental releases of the regulated chemicals for the covered process at this Gas Turbine (Greenville) LLC facility in the past five years.
6.	Emergency Response Program:
Gas Turbine (Greenville) LLC facility has a written Emergency Response Plan that has been established to help safely respond to an accidental release of hazardous substances. The emergency response plan includes procedures for: 
	Clear identification of communication, roles and responsibilities during an emergency event.
	Informing the LEPC about accidental releases that could reasonably result in offsite consequences.
	Providing proper first aid and emergency medical care to treat accidental human exposure to hazardous substances.
	Controlling and containing accidental releases of hazardous substances, including the use of specially trained Hazardous Material Response Teams and emergency response equipment.
	Inspecting and maintaining emergency response equipment.
	Reviewing and updating the emergency response plan.
The Gas Turbine (Greenville) LLC facility maintains an emergency response team that is trained in HAZWOPER, Fire Brigade, and the emergency response procedures. All personnel on site are trained annually for emergency evacuation and shelter in place procedures. Emergency response drills are periodically conducted. The Gas Turbine (Greenville) LLC facility maintains regular contact with the local fire municipalities and involves them in onsite training periodically.

Executive Summary

(Revised in accordance with EPAs requirements for the five-year update.)

1.	Gas Turbine (Greenville) LLC facility Policies
The Gas Turbine (Greenville) LLC facility has developed a compliance program that meets OSHAs PSM regulations and the additional EPA RMP requirements. The documents and management policies address the prevention of an accidental release. The Gas Turbine (Greenville) LLC facility has a fully trained emergency response team with equipment that would respond to such releases and has worked closely with the local responders. Included in the RMP program is the management system, applicable operating, maintenance and response procedures. In addition, the Gas Turbine (Greenville) LLC facility has completed Process Hazard Analysis technical reviews to help ensure equipment and processes will function safely on site. 
2.	Gas Turbine (Greenville) LLC facility Information 
The Gas Turbine (Greenville) LLC facility is a Gas Turbine manufacturing and testing site. The Gas Turbine (Greenville) LLC facility completes combustion testing using a variety of fuels and operating conditions. The testing lab blends different fuels to assess the combustion performance of gas turbines in test cells. Ethane, Butane, Propane, Hydrogen and other substances are stored in tanks and piped to the combustion test cells. Additionally, a Natural Gas line provides fuel to the manufacturing test stands, engineering test stand, and testing lab. Natural gas is used to complete quality checks of the manufactured gas turbines in the manufacturing test stands. 
3.	Worst-Case Scenario/ Alternative Case Scenario
The Gas Turbine (Greenville) LLC facility developed a Worst-case and alternative-case scenario for flammable materials, which identified very minimal impact off the Gas Turbine (Greenville) LLC facility property. These scenarios will be shared with local responders and LEPC to understand the impacts from these scenarios by August 30, 2025.  
4.	Accidental Re

lease Prevention Program
As part of its Accidental Release Prevention Program, Gas Turbine (Greenville) LLC facility complies with the multiple rules and regulations governing the storage, handling and use of the flammable substances. These rules and regulations include for example NFPA 2 and 55, CGA, ASME, API 510, API 570, 29 CFR 1910.103 (Hydrogen) and 1910.106 (Flammable Liquids) and EPA regulations. Implementation of OSHAs PSM and EPAs RMP program provides additional regulatory requirements that help to prevent a release or minimize the impacts if a release occurs. Below are additional programs that have been implemented at the site. 
	Process Safety Information (PSI): A comprehensive set of process safety information has been compiled for the flammable substances. The PSI includes data on the chemicals, the equipment, and the technology of the process. 
	Process Hazards Analysis (PHA): PHAs were conducted on the flammable chemical processes to evaluate potential hazards with the systems as designed. Recommendations were made by the PHA team to help improve the safety of the systems. All safety recommendations are currently being evaluated, and records are being maintained to confirm completion of the recommended actions.  
	Operating Procedures: Operation and Maintenance procedures have been developed to provide, detailed written operating procedures for each of the processes. 
	Training: Training is provided to each operator and maintenance person before they are certified to operate or perform maintenance on the regulated systems.
	Preventative Maintenance: Tanks are maintained by either the supplier company or the Gas Turbine (Greenville) LLC Facility and all internal piping and system are included in the facilitys maintenance program. Equipment inspections, testing and preventive maintenance activities are performed following a structured schedule.

Program (RMP) Requirements: Maintain a Risk Management Plan including hazard assessment, prevention program, and coordinated emergency response procedures, in accordance with 40 CFR Part 68.

These rules require hazardous waste facilities to have a contingency plan designed to minimize hazards to human health and the environment from fires, explosions, or any release of hazardous waste to air, soil, or surface water. 
    Occupational Safety and Health Administration's (OSHA) OSHAs Process Safety Management (PSM) Regulation (29 CFR 1910.119), which contains requirements for preventing or minimizing the consequences of catastrophic releases of toxic, reactive, flammable, or explosive chemicals; specifying that an emergency action plan must be established and implemented for the entire plant  in accordance with the provisions of 29 CFR 1910.38 and that the emergency action plan must include procedures for handling small releases. 
	This Gas Turbine (Greenville) LLC facility is also subject to the hazardous waste and emergency response provisions contained in 29 CFR 1910.120 (a), (p) and (q).

This standard is referenced as part of 49 CFR Part 193 and includes a section on emergency procedures (14.4).

The annual Tier II submittals and dissemination of the Emergency Response Plan and its contents are aligned with the requirement of the EPCRA regulations.
7.	Prevention Program Summary
Gas Turbine (Greenville) LLC facility prevention program focuses on minimizing adverse effects on the health and safety of both plant personnel and its neighbors resulting from unplanned or emergency events. Facilities and equipment are designed and modified in compliance with external codes and standards, preventative maintenance programs as well as internal design practices. Gas Turbine (Greenville

) LLC facility continuously evaluates and improves its accident prevention and emergency response programs through compliance audits and employee participation. Gas Turbine (Greenville) LLC facility fosters an open reporting culture where employees, contractors, and visitors are empowered and encouraged to stop work when unsafe acts or conditions are present.

8.	Planned Changes to Improve Safety: 
Gas Turbine (Greenville) LLC facility continuously strives to improve its safety program and culture by following recommended safe practices, conducting process hazard analysis, reviewing processes though management of change and conducting investigations and implementing mitigation measures in response to incidents. 
The site ensures that PHA action items are addressed and tracked to completion in a timely manner.
